ios-data-display|Charts.summary: The Plenix chart on iOS is a Swift Charts chart in the Plenix frame: a title and a one-sentence takeaway above it, marks in the data-viz colors by the series’ order, light grid lines, tick labels in DM Mono, and the same data as a list or table one tap away. Swift Charts keeps its own layout, scrolling, selection and accessibility (the audio graph and the per-mark VoiceOver labels); Plenix sets the look and the content rules that ChartFrame sets on the web.

anatomy.name: Title
anatomy.about: Names what is measured, in sentence case; it is the chart’s accessibility label.

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.about: One or two sentences with the takeaway, in secondary text; it is the chart’s accessibility value.

anatomy.name: Plot area
anatomy.about: The marks between the axes; the chart’s height comes from the Plenix sizes, its width from the screen.

anatomy.name: Marks
anatomy.about: Bars, lines and points in the data-viz colors, by the series’ order in the data.

anatomy.name: Grid lines and baseline
anatomy.about: Light lines behind the marks; the baseline at zero in the stronger border color.

anatomy.name: Tick labels
anatomy.about: Values, dates and categories in DM Mono, in the reader’s locale.

anatomy.name: Data
anatomy.about: The same values as a list one tap away (Show the data), and the Swift Charts audio graph.

swiftui: /// The Plenix chart frame on iOS: title, takeaway, a Swift Charts plot in the Plenix look, the data one tap away.
/// the plot height: --plx-comp-chart-plot-height-sm, -md or -lg on the web; the library tokens are not generated for iOS yet
// Usage: a column chart; the marks carry their own VoiceOver labels
PlenixChart(title: "Uploads per month", plotHeight: chartPlotHeightMd, takeaway: "Uploads rose from 120 in January to 310 in May.") {
uikit: /// The Plenix chart in UIKit: the SwiftUI chart above, hosted; Swift Charts has no UIKit view of its own.
let host = UIHostingController(rootView: PlenixChart(title: title, plotHeight: chartPlotHeightMd, takeaway: takeaway) { marks })
appkit: // The Plenix chart on the Mac: the same SwiftUI chart in an NSHostingView. A Mac Catalyst app uses the iOS tokens and
// the UIKit code above. A native AppKit app needs a macOS build of PlenixTokens.swift (it uses UIColor today). With it:
let host = NSHostingView(rootView: PlenixChart(title: title, plotHeight: chartPlotHeightMd, takeaway: takeaway) { marks })
